items.followUp: Write HTML code to create a table with two rows and two columns.

rubric.why: Shows the table and row/cell structure.
rubric.description: Names or shows the table, row and data-cell tags.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying or using the basic table structure.

rubric.why: Shows how table entries or headings are placed in cells.
rubric.description: Explains that table data or headings are placed in cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that <td> creates data cells or <th> creates heading cells.

modelAnswer:
Use the tag to start a table and
to end it.
Use and for each row; put cells inside the row using and (or and for heading cells).

items.followUp: What is test data? Explain normal and invalid test data.

rubric.why: Defines test data as data used to check a program.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that test data is input data used to test a program or solution.

rubric.why: Identifies ordinary valid inputs and their purpose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that normal data is valid, typical input expected during ordinary use.

rubric.why: Identifies inputs at the edge of the acceptable range.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that boundary data tests values at or near the limits of the valid range.

rubric.why: Identifies inputs that should not be accepted.
rubric.description: Explains abnormal or invalid test data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that invalid data is outside the allowed conditions and checks how the program handles it.

modelAnswer: Test data is the data entered into a program to check whether it works correctly and produces the expected results.
Normal (valid) test data consists of typical values that the program is designed to accept.
Boundary test data consists of values at or near the limits of the acceptable range.
Invalid (abnormal) test data is outside the acceptable conditions and checks whether the program rejects or handles it correctly.

items.followUp: Name the four TCP/IP layers and describe the function of the Internet layer.

rubric.why: Identifies the Application layer and its role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and stating that it provides network services to applications or users.

rubric.why: Identifies the Transport layer and its role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and describing end-to-end delivery or data segmentation and reliability.

rubric.why: Identifies the Internet layer and its role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and describing logical addressing or routing packets between networks.

rubric.why: Identifies the Network Access layer and its role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and describing transmission of data over the physical network/link.

modelAnswer: The Application layer provides network services to programs and users, such as web and email services.
The Transport layer manages end-to-end communication and may divide data into segments for delivery.
The Internet layer uses logical addresses and routes packets between networks.
The Network Access layer sends and receives data over the physical network link.

items.followUp: Give two differences between an algorithm and a flowchart.

rubric.why: Describes an algorithm as a written sequence of steps.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an algorithm is a step-by-step written procedure.

rubric.why: Describes a flowchart as a visual representation using symbols.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a flowchart represents the solution graphically using standard symbols and arrows.

modelAnswer: An algorithm is a written, step-by-step procedure for solving a problem.
A flowchart is a graphical representation of the solution using standard symbols and arrows.

items.followUp: State two ways testing can help improve a program.

rubric.why: Recognises that testing helps locate errors.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that testing detects errors or bugs in a solution.

rubric.why: Recognises that testing checks whether the solution behaves as intended.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that testing checks expected results or confirms that the program works correctly.

modelAnswer: Testing helps find errors or bugs in a solution.
It checks whether the program gives the expected results and works correctly for its intended inputs.

items.followUp: What is the difference between an ordered list and an unordered list in HTML?

rubric.why: Identifies the kind of list made by the tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that <ul> creates an unordered list, usually displayed with bullets.

rubric.why: Explains how entries are added to the list.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that each list entry is written using the <li> tag.

modelAnswer: The <ul> tag creates an unordered list, usually displayed with bullet points.
Each entry in the list is written inside an <li> tag.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of the head section of an HTML page?

rubric.why: Names the page's head section and a typical item it contains.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the head as a main part of the web page and mentioning information such as the title or metadata.

rubric.why: Names the body section and explains its role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the body as the part containing the page content displayed in the browser.

modelAnswer: The two main parts of an HTML web page are the head and the body.
The head contains page information such as the title; the body contains the content displayed in the browser.

items.followUp: Define a numeral system and name the digits used in the decimal system.

rubric.why: Defines a number system as a way to represent numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a number system is a method or system for representing numbers.

rubric.why: Mentions the symbols or rules used in representing numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning digits/symbols and/or rules such as place value.

modelAnswer: A number system is a method of representing numbers using a set of digits or symbols and rules for their use.
The value of a digit may depend on its position in the number.
